study: The sooner %R open: lines still apart, both rising toward 0, gap closing, against the next 3 minutes.
registered_at: 2026-10-17, before any return of this rule was computed.
origin: Operator 2026-10-17, after the PPL, SHEL, and UNH charts. The prediction is generally correct, not perfect. Lines still more than about 15 points apart, both rising toward 0, and the gap closing, means the price is already rising, and that minute is sooner than waiting for the lines to meet. The live book refuses that minute because the gap is still wider than 15. This test is that prediction. It is not a rerun of pr_path, and it is not the pr_dir5 cell (any 5-minute rise, anywhere on the scale).
charts_are_not_the_sample: The shape was read off PPL, SHEL, and UNH on 2026-10-16, which is after the last warehouse day, and off PPL's 2026-10-15 afternoon, which is inside half B. No coefficient was fit. The 15-point gap and the 20-point top band are the live desk's existing confluence and overbought level. The 5-minute history is the direction window already named by the operator. None of those numbers is searched on the warehouse.

same_page.gap: Fast line minus slow line, in points. The apart test and the closing test use the absolute gap. Positive means the fast line is above the slow line. Not a price gap.
same_page.still_apart: Absolute gap now is strictly wider than 15 points. 15 is the live tight level. A gap of 15 or less is the arrival, which this test does not call.
same_page.both_rising_toward_zero: Both lines are below 0 now, and each line is strictly higher than it was 5 minutes ago. Higher on this scale is toward 0. A line sitting at 0 is not still approaching. A line that fell is not rising.
same_page.gap_closing: The absolute gap now is strictly smaller than the absolute gap 5 minutes ago. An unchanged gap is not closing.
same_page.the_case: All three at once, at the close of minute m: still apart, both rising toward 0, gap closing. That is the only call.
same_page.forward: The lines are read at the close of minute m. The return starts at the SIP open of minute m+1 and ends at the SIP close of minute m+3. The 5-minute history uses only minute m and minute m-5. A later minute is not read. Yesterday's reading is not an input.
same_page.pictures: Two pictures are printed and are not the call. Fast leaving the top: the fast line was at or above -20 five minutes ago and is lower now. Close and flat: the absolute gap is 15 or less and neither line moved by more than 1 point over those 5 minutes. The 1-point band is the definition of flat for that picture. It is not searched, and the grade does not read it. The share of call minutes whose gross return is positive is also a picture. Promoting either picture is a new prereg.
same_page.causation: The lines are computed from prices that have already printed. This test can show whether that picture lines up with the next 3 minutes. It cannot show that the lines cause the move.

prior: The 10-minute path test mixed every line position and came out at about 0.0 bp gross. The live square waits until the lines are already within 15 points and near the top, and that arrival was gross-negative at a 10-minute hold. Neither one is this rule at a 3-minute hold.
data: Same warehouse and sample as pr_path: 119 sessions 2026-04-28..2026-10-15, 400 names per session seeded sha256(day|prescreen-sample), names with today's IEX, today's SIP, and the previous session's IEX. The parent list is the prior day's liquid names, not today's watchlist. IEX for the lines, SIP for the return. A SIP result is not assumed to transfer to an IEX fill. Lines warmed on the previous session. The causal minute grid from pr_path is reused: at most 14 flat minutes forward from a real print, no look at the next print, no overnight fill. The run refuses unless n = 119, first = 2026-04-28, last = 2026-10-15, and the median split is 2026-07-23.
window: Minutes 09:35 through 15:56 ET. 09:35 is the first minute with a 5-minute history inside the regular session. 15:56 is the last minute whose 3-minute return ends on the 15:59 close.
split: Half A is sessions on or before 2026-07-23. Half B is sessions after 2026-07-23. The bar below is applied to each half. A pass on one half is not a pass.
call: One call, on the approach cell, on the next 3 minutes, net of 10 bp (E.COST). PROMISING only if EACH half has net > 0, day-clustered t of the net day-means >= 1.5, excess versus the other minutes that day > 0 with day-clustered t >= 1.5, and excess versus the other names at that same minute > 0 with day-clustered t >= 1.5, with at least 30 cell-days, 30 excess days, 30 cross days, and 1000 cell-minutes on that half. A flat 10 bp toll is charged on every minute, so it cancels in the excess and in the cross; those two tests stay on the gross difference. The level test is the day's approach mean minus 10 bp. A missing t, either half short of 30 days or 1000 minutes or 30 excess days or 30 cross days, or indicator failures above 1% of sampled name-days, is UNDERPOWERED. Anything else is FAIL. There is no PASS. PROMISING is a paper reading of this written rule. It does not change config. The pictures are not a second call. 3 bp is printed because that is the capped book's round trip. The grade does not read 3 bp.
why_not_a_later_minute_control: Scoring every minute makes a later minute of the same name overlap a 3-minute hold. The controls are the other minutes that day, and the other names at the same minute.
no_retuning: The 15-point apart level, the requirement that both lines be below 0 and higher than 5 minutes ago, the closing test, the 3-minute hold, the 10 bp toll, the window, the sample, and the 2026-07-23 split are fixed. A different history length, a different apart level, or a call on either picture is a new prereg.
command: On the mini, after a result-skeptic Mode 1 READY, and only then: scp tools/studies/pr_approach.py and tools/studies/pr_path.py to /tmp, then REPO=$PWD nice -n 19 .venv/bin/python /tmp/pr_approach.py --score. No pytest over SSH. No config edit.
